title: Add Tidewater to the comparison page
prompt:
The co-branded comparison page shows both brands side by side, each in a section with its own `data-brand`. Add the Tidewater brand **without touching the component rules**:

- headings use the Georgia font stack (`--nw-font-georgia`),
- buttons are pills (`999px` radius),
- the button background is `--nw-teal-700`, because teal-600 fails contrast with white text,
- the Northwind section must stay exactly as it is.

Right now the semantic tier is only declared on `:root`. Think about where it gets resolved.
hints: Write a `[data-brand="tidewater"] { … }` block that points the brand tokens (`--nw-brand-font-heading`, `--nw-brand-radius-control` and the ramp) at Tidewater values.
Brand tokens alone won't reach the section: the semantic tokens were computed on `:root` with Northwind's values. Change the semantic rule's selector to `:root, [data-brand]`.
Inside the Tidewater block, also map `--nw-color-action-bg` to `var(--nw-brand-700)`.
explanation: The brand block only swaps brand-tier values, plus one semantic mapping that Tidewater genuinely needs for contrast. Re-declaring the semantic tier under `[data-brand]` is what makes each section compute `--nw-color-action-bg`, `--nw-font-heading` and `--nw-radius-control` from its own brand tokens, instead of inheriting values already resolved at the root. The components never mention a brand, so a third brand is one more block.

checks.northwind-intact: The Northwind section keeps its blue button, 6px radius and Inter headings
checks.tidewater-contrast: Tidewater buttons use teal-700 with white text
checks.no-brand-in-components: No rule targets components by brand
